question.text: Three members of the House of Medici went on to hold this office in Rome, taking the names Leo X, Clement VII, and Leo XI.
question.answerHtml: Pope [or “the papacy;” or Supreme Pontiff; or Pontifex Maximus; or Bishop of Rome]
question.clue: Conquests by Aisulf, king of the Lombards, led a holder of this position to journey across the Alps to request aid, after which lands conquered by a Frankish king were given to holders of this position by the Donation of Pepin.

swap.text: This pope, who served during World War II, has been called "Hitler's Pope" for not doing enough to stop the Holocaust.
swap.clue: While on trial, Karl Wolff testified that he had been ordered to kidnap this leader, who gave a "Christmas Broadcast" in support of one group who had "been consigned to death or to a slow decline".

question.leadin: This term sometimes refers to the period of antipopes during the Avignon Papacy.
question.text: Name this term which also applies to an exile of Jews from Judah begun by Nebuchadnezzar and ended by Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: This period in which Philip IV of France moved the Papacy to Avignon, named after a duration of time in the Old Testament.

swap.leadin: Due to their military-like structure, members of this group are sometimes called "God's Marines."
swap.text: Name this Catholic religious order founded by Ignatius Loyola. Members of this group included Francis Xavier, who traveled to Japan as a missionary.
swap.clue: Two members of this group prepared the translation of the Treaty of Nerchinsk and another created a lunisolar calendar for the last Ming emperor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the investiture controversy.
question.text: The controversy over appointing bishops was sparked by the reforms launched by the seventh pope of this name. The thirteenth pope of this name created the modern calendar.
question.clue: Those two theologians with this name are from Nyssa and Nazianzus, and are considered "Cappadocian fathers" along with Basil the Great.

swap.leadin: Pope Martin V was elected following this ecumenical council, which also condemned Jan Hus as a heretic.
swap.text: Name this 15th century council, which ended the Western Schism.
swap.clue: It was here that Pope Gregory XII helped elect Oddone Colonna as his own replacement.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of Malta.
question.text: This Christian military order ruled Malta for over two and a half centuries, until Ferdinand von Hompesch zu Bolheim surrendered it to Napoleon in 1798.
question.answerHtml: Knights Hospitaller [or Knights of Saint John, accept Order in place of “Knights” in either]
question.clue: This group was founded by merchants from Amalfi, and was later led by Gerard Thom.

swap.leadin: Terrorists planned to assassinate this pope during a visit to the Philippines in the first phase of the Bojinka Plot.
swap.text: Name this pope who established World Youth Day in 1985. This pope's visit to his home country motivated the formation of the Solidarity movement, which went on to end communist rule in that country.
swap.clue: This man made a prison visit to forgive Mehmet Ali Agca, a member of the Grey Wolves who tried to kill him.

question.leadin: This pope officially established the Swiss Guard and rose to power as a mediator between the Orsini and Colonna families.
question.text: Identify this "warrior pope" and patron of Michelangelo.
question.clue: Louis XII convened a conciliabulum at Pisa against this ruler, though earlier this ruler had allied with France, Spain, and the Holy Roman Empire against Venice, forming the League of Cambrai.

swap.text: This future Pope, the first to resign from the Papacy in nearly six hundred years, served as a theological consultant at Vatican II.
swap.answerHtml: Benedict XVI [or Joseph Aloisius Ratzinger; prompt on partial answers]
swap.clue: Other critics of this man attacked his lavish dress, for which he was known as "the pope of aesthetics," while others were upset by his conscription into Germany's military in World War II.

question.text: This order of warrior monks took oaths to protect pilgrims to Jerusalem. They derive their name from the location of their treasury in Jerusalem.
question.clue: This organization triumphed at the Battle of Montgisard, while members of this organization captured at the Battle of Hattin were executed by Saladin.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an early show trial.
swap.text: The trials were conducted by Guillaume de Nogart, chancellor to Philip IV of France, whose other power grabs included moving the Papacy to this French city in 1309.
swap.clue: Six elections were held in this city's Palais des Papes during a period alternately called the "Babylonian Captivity."

question.text: The fifth pope to take this name suppressed the Templars at the Council of Vienne and moved the papacy to Avignon, thus beginning the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: He rescinded an earlier papal bull which proclaimed that outside of the church, there is no salvation.

swap.text: One of these splits in the Christian church arose when Gregory XI moved the papacy back to Rome. The split between the Orthodox and Catholic church in 1054 is known as the "Great" one of these.
swap.clue: This breaks and splits in the Christian church. The "Great" one resulted in the formation of the Catholic Church, while the "Western" one saw three popes ruling simultaneously.

question.leadin: Identify the following ecumenical councils from their theological statements.
question.text: This unrecognized council of 1409 failed to end the Western Schism, and its decision was superseded by the later Council of Constance.
question.clue: Philargi was elected and took the name Alexander V, but the results were ignored since Urban VI and Clement VII both refused to recognize this council.

swap.leadin: This pope probably died of injuries associated with a painful fall from his mule at Narni.
swap.text: This 14th century Pope once complained that he couldn't hear enough screaming when some rebellious cardinals were being tortured. He was opposed by Antipope Clement VII during the Western Schism.

question.text: Much of the discussion at Ferrara-Florence centered upon this Latin phrase, whose presence in the Nicene Creed was rejected by the Eastern Orthodox church. It describes the origin of the Holy Spirit.
question.clue: The addition in question was this clause in the Nicene creed which translates to "from the Father and the Son." In greek, this clause had a literal one iota difference from the Orthodox preferred version.

swap.text: Saint Catherine of Siena persuaded this pope to move the papacy back to Rome. This pope also hired John Hawkwood to fight on his behalf in the War of the Eight Saints.
swap.answerHtml: Pope <u>Gregory XI</u> [or Pierre-Roger de <u>Beaufort</u>; prompt on “<u>Gregory</u>”]

question.leadin: Their ranks include St. Hippolytus of Rome, Novatian, Anastasius, and Anacletus II, while more notable individuals to hold this dubious distinction include Robert of Geneva and Benedict XIII.
question.text: Name the position held by all of these individuals, the later two of which resided in Avignon during the Great Western Schism.
question.clue: Clement VII was the first of two of these popes, who are not considered official by the Roman Catholic Church. Modern groups of them include the Sedevacantist ones and the Conclavist ones.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about historical cross-dressers, FTPE.
swap.text: Between the time of Popes Sergius III and John XII, the Vatican church went through this period which saw all sorts of accusations of crossdressing, under the direction of Theodora and the Theophylacti. This time also witnessed a Cadaver Synod.
swap.clue: In addition to John X, this period saw the reign of Lando, and much of the information known about this period comes from the writings of Liutprand of Cremona.
